Bulgaria lights up its Black Sea coast with digital art festival Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 11/08/2026 - 18:01 GMT+2 Bulgaria’s southern Black Sea coast became an open‑air gallery from 7 to 10 August, as the second LUNAR: Sea of Lights festival brought 17 light and digital artworks to five seaside communities. … More Installations and projection shows illuminated buildings, fields, beaches and the sea in Tsarevo, Varvara, Ahtopol and Sinemorets. Artists from eight countries took part, combining contemporary art with the coastal landscape after sunset. The programme ran each evening from 9 p.m. to midnight and was free to the public, with video mapping, interactive installations, lasers and large‑scale light compositions transforming familiar urban and natural sites into a continuous night‑time route.bnrnews+3 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT In Varvara, MP‑STUDIO projected its “Time Harvest” installation onto hay bales in the meadow above the beach, while Latvian artists Those Guys Lighting presented “Divine Geometry” and other works in the same open field, turning the grassy slope into a luminous landscape. In Ahtopol, “Endless Currents” used the shoreline and the changing surface of the sea as a projection surface, with waves and tides becoming part of the moving image.bnrnews+1 Tsarevo hosted several works, including “Gifts of the Sea”, a video mapping show on the façade of the Georgi Kondolov Community Hall, and “The Moon”, the festival’s symbol, displayed as a light installation near the Ship Fountain. Mayor Marin Kirov said the first seaside edition had drawn a record number of visitors and that the 2026 event had been expanded with more locations and installations, including the new stop in Varvara. In Sinemorets, the light installation “For Peace” by Slovak artist sedemminut was presented in a meadow overlooking the beach, featuring glowing human figures that appeared to run through the darkness in a message of peace, freedom and artistic expression. Organisers said the festival aims to connect people with nature while attracting visitors interested in contemporary art, building on the success of the original LUNAR festival in Sofia, which has attracted hundreds of thousands of spectators since its launch in 2022. https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/15/at-l.text: Istanbul was battling to recover from flooding caused by what officials said on Thursday was the heaviest rainfall in the city since records began more than 80 years ago, as the downpour continued.The rain began lashing Turkey's largest city in earnest on Wednesday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters."We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942," Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.Two people died in the floods, one of them a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area. He was rushed to hospital but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said.Another three people were being treated in hospital, Gul said.On Wednesday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home "unless absolutely necessary" and advising those living in basement properties "to spend the night on safer, higher floors".He advised residents to stay away from "stream beds, underpasses and other areas at risk of flooding".Dramatic footage posted online and collated by DHA news agency showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.Forty-three flights bound for Istanbul Airport on the Black Sea had to be diverted, as did three flights heading for the city's Sabiha Gökçen airport on the Asian side, which also temporarily suspended take-offs due to strong winds, the transport ministry said in a statement carried by state news agency Anadolu.Turkey's AFAD disaster agency has set up a crisis desk to manage incidents caused by the heavy rainfall, which by nightfall Wednesday had risen to 1,277 flooding incidents, 15 landslides, 47 people stranded and two roofs blown off.The heavy rains are expected to continue over the weekend.

https://www.demingheadlight.com/2026/10/.text: tap News Sports Business Opinion Entertainment E-Edition News Sports Business Opinion Entertainment E-Edition Events October 8, 2026 Klobase time Article by Billy Armendariz, Deming Headlight Church festival tickets on sale By Billy Armendariz Headlight Staff Plans are moving rapidly for the annual Holy Family Catholic Church Klobase Festival. The first order of business is selling tickets for the festival’s barbecue, slated for Sunday, Oct. 18, at Luna County Courthouse Park in Deming. Tickets are $12 and include beef brisket, klobase sausage, potato salad, cole slaw and beans. Serving is from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the courthouse park pavilion. Tickets can be purchased at the Holy Family Parish Office, 615 S. Copper St,. or from any parishioner. The office also now accepts credit cards. The Luna County Old Timers’ Association will once against play a part in the celebration. The 112th Old Timers’ Reunion is slated for the same weekend, and many former Deming residents who return for the reunion are expected to be at Courthouse Park. “This is great time to reconnect with family and friends,” said Holy Family parishioner Paul Sanchez. “The festival is also our main fundraising event for the parish.” Holy Family Catholic Church has celebrated the Czech harvest festival for the past 98 years in Deming. A migration of Texas Czech families in the 1920s came to southern New Mexico for the promise of fertile farmland and the opportunity to homestead. The church became that beacon of promise, and each year farmers, ranchers and parishioners would celebrate the harvest with the Klobase Festival. Through the years, the volunteers have prepared and served plates and provided a dessert table, cold drinks, activities for kids and music. There will also be bingo games in the afternoon. Luna County Old Timers is considered one of the longest- standing social gathering in all of New Mexico. The organization was formed when former students returned annually to attend class reunions. The idea of a single reunion weekend flourished as membership for the organization grew each year. Class reunions are set up by decade, and there is one dinner and dance that invites all members to party. That dinner and dance will be held beginning at 5:30 on Saturday, Oct. 17, at the Mimbres Valley Special Events Center, 2300 E. Pine St. Tickets are $30 per person and can be purchased at the door. “Our community has always been so generous in supporting the festival,” Sanchez noted. “Having the families from the Old Timers’ Association creates a chance for memories with other families, and a boost for our church.” Above, Paul Sanchez and Rev. Prakasham Babu of Holy Family Catholic Church sell the first ticket to this year’s Klobase Festival to incoming Luna County Old Timers’ Association co-presidents Duane Ruebush, Cecelia Ruebush and Deloris Ruebush Hawkins. At right, klobase sausage is cooked at Luna County Courthouse Park over a wood-burning cooker each year. (Headlight Staff Photo by Billy Armendariz) If you go… Who: Holy Family Catholic Church parish What: 98th annual Klobase Festival When: Sunday, Oct. 18 Where: Luna County Courthouse Park, 700 S. Silver Ave. Why: Church and community celebrates the history of the Czech harvest and raises funds for the church. Tickets: Klobase and beef brisket plates $12, available at the Holy Family Parish Ofice s S Copper St or from any parishioner.
